caption: React state is the information a component remembers between renders. Change the state, and React rebuilds the visible result from that new information.

slides.title: WHAT IS
slides.subtitle: The information your interface needs to remember.

slides.title: VALUE OR
slides.subtitle: Not every variable belongs in component state.

items.label: STATE
items.text: Information that changes what users see

slides.prompt: ASK: SHOULD THE UI REMEMBER THIS?

slides.title: THE REACT
slides.subtitle: User actions change data, then data changes the view.

slides.title: A COUNTER
slides.subtitle: The interface remembers the current count.

slides.title: STATE SHOULD
slides.subtitle: Too much state creates synchronization problems.

items.label: KEEP CLOSE
items.text: Place state near the component using it

items.label: LIFT ONLY
items.text: Share state when multiple parts need it

caption: Responsive design is not shrinking a desktop page. It is deciding what should reflow, resize, hide or become easier to tap as space changes.

slides.title: RESPONSIVE IS
slides.subtitle: The layout must adapt, not merely squeeze.

slides.title: FOUR THINGS
slides.subtitle: Review each layer at every major width.
slides.prompt: TEST THE SYSTEM, NOT ONE SCREEN

slides.title: FIXED OR
slides.subtitle: Choose values based on what should adapt.

items.label: FIXED
items.text: Borders, icons and minimum tap sizes

slides.title: LET TYPE
slides.subtitle: Set a minimum, fluid middle and maximum.

slides.title: BEFORE YOU
slides.subtitle: Check the experience, not only the screenshot.

caption: Sorting algorithms can produce the same result while doing very different amounts of work. This carousel compares the intuition behind bubble sort and merge sort.

slides.title: SAME LIST.
slides.subtitle: Two sorting strategies can finish with very different effort.

slides.title: BUBBLE SORT:
slides.subtitle: Large values repeatedly move toward the end.

items.label: 2  SWAP
items.text: Move them if out of order

slides.title: MERGE SORT:
slides.subtitle: Small sorted groups are easier to combine.

slides.title: SMALL INPUT.
slides.subtitle: Both work, but scale changes the cost.

items.label: BUBBLE SORT
items.text: Easy to understand; slow on large lists

items.label: MERGE SORT
items.text: More structure; efficient as data grows

slides.title: DON'T MEMORIZE
slides.subtitle: Ask how the algorithm reduces the remaining work.

caption: A model can reach 99 percent accuracy and still fail the task you care about. When classes are unbalanced, inspect precision, recall and the confusion matrix.

slides.title: 99% ACCURATE.
slides.subtitle: A high score can hide the exact failures that matter.

slides.title: IMAGINE 100
slides.subtitle: Only one message contains dangerous content.

slides.title: PRECISION OR
slides.subtitle: The right metric depends on the cost of each mistake.

items.label: PRECISION
items.text: When the model flags it, how often is it right?

items.label: RECALL
items.text: How much of the real danger did it find?

slides.prompt: CHOOSE THE METRIC FOR THE GOAL

slides.title: READ THE
slides.subtitle: Four outcomes reveal what accuracy hides.

slides.title: BEFORE SHARING
slides.subtitle: Give the audience enough context to judge it.

items.label: BASELINE
items.text: What happens with a simple guess?

items.label: METRIC
items.text: Why does this score match the goal?

slides.prompt: REPORT THE STORY BEHIND THE NUMBER

caption: Do not ask only whether an AI answer sounds good. Ask whether the claims are traceable, the code runs and independent evidence agrees. Use this five-step verification workflow.

slides.title: AI ANSWERED.
slides.subtitle: A response becomes useful only after you inspect it.

slides.title: CHECK THE
slides.subtitle: Separate facts, opinions and assumptions.

items.label: SOURCE
items.text: Can you open the original evidence?

slides.title: IF IT GIVES CODE,
slides.subtitle: Never trust a large generated solution all at once.

slides.title: ONE ANSWER OR
slides.subtitle: Agreement only matters when sources do not copy each other.

items.label: STRONG CHECK
items.text: Compare documentation, data or direct tests

slides.title: USE AI AS
slides.subtitle: Keep human judgment at the final decision.
slides.prompt: THINK WITH AI. DO NOT OUTSOURCE THINKING.

caption: A strong project case study helps someone understand the problem, your decisions and what changed because of your work. Use this five-slide structure for your next portfolio entry.

slides.title: TURN A PROJECT
slides.subtitle: A screenshot shows the result. A case study shows your thinking.
slides.prompt: SWIPE FOR THE CASE STUDY FRAME

slides.title: START WITH
slides.subtitle: Give the reader a reason to care before showing features.

slides.title: SHOW THE
slides.subtitle: Explain the reasoning that cannot be seen in a screenshot.

items.label: TEST
items.text: How did you check the result?

slides.title: FEATURE LIST OR
slides.subtitle: Describe what improved for the user or the project.

items.label: STRONG
items.text: Users can find saved notes in fewer steps

slides.title: END WITH
slides.subtitle: Reflection proves you can evaluate your own work.

caption: Seven days will not make you an expert, but they can give you momentum and a finished mini project. Follow this plan for one focused hour per day.

slides.title: START PYTHON
slides.subtitle: One focused hour each day. One project at the end.

slides.title: DAYS 1-2:
slides.subtitle: Make programs that receive and remember information.
slides.prompt: TYPE IT. CHANGE IT. EXPLAIN IT.

slides.title: DAYS 3-4:
slides.subtitle: Make the program choose and repeat.

slides.title: DAYS 5-6:
slides.subtitle: Organize information and reusable logic.
slides.prompt: GIVE DATA AND LOGIC A STRUCTURE

slides.title: DAY 7:
slides.subtitle: Combine the week into one finished project.

slides.title: THE DAILY
slides.subtitle: Use the same process every day.

slides.title: AFTER DAY 7:
slides.subtitle: Use the project to choose the next skill.

caption: Error messages are not insults. They are compressed clues. Learn to identify the error type, file, line and final message before searching for a solution.

slides.title: THE ERROR MESSAGE
slides.subtitle: Read it from the bottom, then trace the path upward.

slides.title: START WITH
slides.subtitle: It usually names the error and the immediate problem.
code: TypeError: can only join str to str
slides.prompt: DO NOT SEARCH THE WHOLE TRACE

slides.title: TURN THE MESSAGE
slides.subtitle: A clear question leads to a focused test.

items.label: 1  EXPECT
items.text: What type did the code need?

slides.title: SEARCH LESS.
slides.subtitle: Keep the meaningful error terms and remove personal data.

items.label: BETTER SEARCH
items.text: Python TypeError join str to str

slides.prompt: SEARCH THE ERROR, NOT THE EMOTION

slides.title: BEFORE ASKING
slides.subtitle: Bring enough evidence for someone to reproduce it.

caption: Good database design begins with real objects and relationships, not random columns. Model the things your application needs to remember and give each record a stable identity.

slides.title: DESIGN THE DATA
slides.subtitle: Start with the real-world objects your app must remember.

slides.title: A HABIT APP
slides.subtitle: Each object becomes a candidate for its own table.

slides.title: CONNECT WITH
slides.subtitle: Relationships should not depend on names that can change.

slides.title: ONE FIELD OR
slides.subtitle: Repeated groups often deserve their own table.

items.label: FRAGILE
items.text: Store every check-in inside one text field

slides.prompt: DESIGN FOR THE QUESTIONS YOU WILL ASK

slides.title: BEFORE CREATING
slides.subtitle: Test the model using real actions from the app.

items.label: CREATE
items.text: Can a user add a habit?

items.label: READ
items.text: Can the app show today's habits?

slides.prompt: MODEL THE FULL DATA LIFE CYCLE

caption: Deployment is part of development. Before sharing your URL, test the production build, mobile layout, links, loading states and metadata.

slides.title: YOUR SITE WORKS
slides.subtitle: Now make sure it works for everyone else.
slides.prompt: SWIPE BEFORE YOU SHARE THE URL

slides.title: CHECK THE
slides.subtitle: Development mode can hide problems users will see.

slides.title: TEST THE
slides.subtitle: Use another device and a fresh browser session.
slides.prompt: DO NOT TEST ONLY THE HAPPY PATH

slides.title: MAKE THE LINK
slides.subtitle: A polished preview earns more clicks and trust.

items.label: DESCRIPTION
items.text: Explain the page in one sentence

slides.prompt: DETAILS MAKE THE PROJECT FEEL FINISHED
